# A window under `if details` is a node in a render slot: created each time
# `details` turns true and destroyed each time it turns false, content and
# effects with it. The timer turns it on, off and on again, so gtk4's Wayland
# log shows its toplevel created twice, and the effect in its body -- which
# lives as long as the window -- mounts twice and unmounts once, on both
# hosts. Nothing in it survives the condition turning false: the counter in
# its body starts again at zero the second time.
#
# testdata/window_under_if.txtar is the code.

[!headless] skip 'needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

[gtk4] sngl build --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl
[gtk4] exec sh -c 'WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./gtk4/app 2>&1 | grep -c "xdg_toplevel.*set_title(\"Load\")" || true'
[gtk4] stdout '^2$'
[gtk4] exec ./gtk4/app
[gtk4] cmp stdout want.txt

sngl build --lang go --platform fyne -o fyne app.sngl
exec ./fyne/app
cmp stdout want.txt

-- want.txt --
mounted 1
unmounted
mounted 1
-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

#[go.native("fmt", "fmt.Println")]
func println(s string)

var (
    details = false
    ticks = 0
)

time.timer(interval=200ms, @tick {
    ticks += 1
    if ticks <= 3 {
        details = !details
    }
    if ticks == 5 {
        exit(0)
    }
})

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.text(value="{ticks}")
}

if details {
    ui.window(title="Load", @closed {
        details = false
    }) {
        ui.text(value="load")
        counter()
    }
}

component counter ui.node {
    var mounts = 0
    ui.text(value="{mounts}")
    effect(@mount {
        mounts += 1
        println("mounted {mounts}")
    }, @unmount {
        println("unmounted")
    })
}
